turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung scolded O-lan, accusing her of foolishness and insisting that she was not going anywhere, that he would not let her leave.
turns.speech: What foolishness are you talking, O-lan? You are not going anywhere, I will not let you go anywhere!

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid had not meant to intrude, but she was wondering if she could be of some help to O-lan, as O-lan had said, she should look to her husband and his family.
turns.speech: I, um, I did not mean to intrude, Mother, but I was wondering if I could be of some help to you, as you, as you said, I should look to my husband and his family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan knew that Wang Lung would not let her leave, but she was tired, and she must think of her son's future. He needed a wife, a woman to take care of him, and she must see him married and settled before she went.
turns.speech: O-lan knows that Wang Lung will not let me leave, but I am tired, and I must think of my son's future. He needs a wife, a woman to take care of him, and I must see him married and settled before I go.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He told O-lan, please don't worry about him, he'd be fine, and he'd make sure to take care of himself.
turns.speech: Mother, please don't worry about me, I'll be fine, and I'll make sure to take care of myself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: But she must see him married, for his sake, her son.
turns.speech: But I must see him married, for your sake, my son.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was frantic, he exclaimed, and he would not let O-lan leave him. He swore to take care of her, his wife, his companion, and he would not let her go.
turns.speech: O-lan, you will not leave me! I will not let you go! You are my wife, my companion, and I will take care of you, I swear it!

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He told O-lan, don't worry, he'd be fine, he promised. He'd make sure to take care of himself and their family's fields.
turns.speech: Mother, don't worry, I'll be fine, I promise. I'll make sure to take care of myself and our family's fields.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was old, and her body was weak. She must see him married, her son, before she went.
turns.speech: I am old, and my body is weak. I must see you married, my son, before I go.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid had brought warm water for O-lan to wash with, if she'd like.
turns.speech: Mother, I've brought warm water for you to wash with, if you'd like.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's thoughts turned to her son, and she knew it was not for her to be taken care of, but for him. He must be married, and have children of his own, so that she could finally rest.
turns.speech: It is not for me to be taken care of, but for my son. He must be married, and have children of his own.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He was worried, he told O-lan, and he would take care of everything. He would find a good wife and start a new life, just like Father wanted.
turns.speech: Mother, please, don't worry about me, I'll take care of everything. I'll find a good wife and start a new life, just like Father wants.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's voice was firm, his eyes burning with determination, as he spoke to O-lan: he would not lose their son, he swore it to her. He would see him married, with children of his own, and their family's fields would flourish, just as she had always wanted.
turns.speech: O-lan, I will not lose our son, I swear it to you. He will be married, he will have children, and our family's fields will be prosperous, just as you want.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was tired, but she would not rest until she saw her eldest son married.
turns.speech: I am tired, but I will not rest until I see you married, my son.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked if she could bring O-lan some food, O-lan must eat something to keep his strength up.
turns.speech: May I bring you some food, O-lan? You must eat something to keep your strength up.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was not hungry, the child.
turns.speech: I am not hungry, child

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid was so sorry, but perhaps O-lan should rest now. The sun was setting, and it wasn't good for her to be up.
turns.speech: I'm so sorry, Mother, but perhaps you should rest now. The sun is setting, and it's not good for you to be up

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan would not rest now, she told the maid, she must see to the wedding preparations.
turns.speech: I will not rest now, daughter. I must see to the wedding preparations.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid was eager to assist, she said, and her hands were steady, so she could take some of the burden off O-lan, if she insisted on seeing to the wedding preparations.
turns.speech: If you insist on seeing to the wedding preparations, O-lan, perhaps I could help you with something. My hands are steady, and I could take some of the burden off you.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan would not burden the maid with this, child. It was her duty to see to the wedding preparations, and she would not rest until it was done.
turns.speech: I will not burden you with this, child. It is my duty to see to the wedding preparations, and I will not rest until it is done.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid begged O-lan not to overexert herself, her health not as it was, and she feared for O-lan's well-being.
turns.speech: But, O-lan, please, I beg of you, do not overexert yourself. Your health is not as it was, and I fear for your well-being.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
